summary: The replace module replaces all matches of a regex in a file; you must keep it idempotent by ensuring replacements don't match again. before/after combined work correctly since 2.7.10.
questions: How do I replace every occurrence of a string in a file?
How do I keep replace idempotent?
Did before and after behave differently in older Ansible?

answer_card.title: Replace text across a file
answer_card.answer_md: `ansible.builtin.replace` replaces **all** regex matches in a file. Ensure the replacement can't match the pattern again, or it won't be idempotent. `before`+`after` together work correctly since 2.7.10.
